correctness.rationale: Born probabilities of symmetric open-chain MPS |ψ_{n,g}> are g^{D(x)}/[2(1+g)^{n−1}], giving independent original wall Bernoulli θ=g/(1+g). The XOR of two independent words has fair initial bit and independent wall probability h=2g/(1+g)². Pair Z_iZ_j noise multiplies off-diagonal x,y by 1−2a_{j−i} iff XOR bits at i,j differ; squaring gives exact purity E_U ∏_r |1−2a_r|^{2C_r(U)}. At g_n=λ/n, K_n~Bin(n−1,h_n)→Poisson(2λ). For each finite k, random wall positions are asymptotically separated and interior in the sense of first fixing ε>0, controlling exceptional configurations, then letting ε↓0; for distances below separation C_r=kr; for all r, C_r≤kr. At α>2, log tails ∑r^{1−α} converge giving q=∏|1−2p/r^α|^{2r}; for α<1 or 1<α≤2, a positive fraction of crossing attenuation diverges and conditional product→0 for k≥1. Averaging Poisson generating function gives exp[−2λ(1−q)]. At α=2,p_n=c/log n, ΣC_r/r²=k log n+O_k(1), log weight→−4ck, hence crossover exp[−2λ(1−e^{−4c})]. p=0, p=1/2 and nearest-neighbor finite-size checks handled. The proof needs ε→0 rather than claim fixed-ε separation has probability 1; the formulation supports that limiting argument. Inspected MPS/density-matrix verifier and independently checked C_r=kr for isolated wall small r at n=20,80; finite tests do not prove limits.

value.rationale: The weak-fugacity g_n≈λ/n scaling is a natural dilute-defect regime approaching the GHZ point, and exact nonzero global purity has direct consequences for the feasibility of measuring Rényi-2 observables. The result distinguishes summable/noisy regimes and an inverse-log marginal transition quantitatively for a motivated quantum channel; it explicitly does not prove mixed-phase persistence or state preparation at a fixed thermodynamic phase.

limitations: Special g≥0 symmetric open-chain MPS; pair noise commuting; α=1 undefined; λ,c fixed limits; no uniformity over parameters.
Nonzero purity limit does not establish mixed SPT order, phase stability, decoding advantage or controlled finite-g thermodynamic phase.
